organizations.What they build: German motion-technology supplier (bearings, drives). Now sells parts for humanoid robot joints: an actuator is the 'muscle' of a joint (motor + gearbox + sensor). In Aug 2026 it announced formed strain wave gearboxes (compact, high-ratio gears; actuators are about half of a humanoid's cost). It is also a big buyer: UK startup Humanoid will put a four-digit number of robots in Schaeffler factories and buy a seven-digit number of Schaeffler actuators.
organizations._relationship_reason: Huge corporate pushing humanoid actuators; a lab could at best get a talk or a small sponsorship via its humanoid/innovation teams; hardware donations unlikely.

organizations.What they build: Swiss maker of precision DC/brushless motors, gearheads, encoders and motor controllers (e.g. ESCON2 servo controllers). At Automate 2026 it showed IP67 integrated drives and an integrated joint actuator for humanoids. Its motors are common in research robots and Mars rovers.
organizations._relationship_reason: Has a 'Young Engineers Program' listed on its site that supports student projects with drives; realistic route to discounted motors.

organizations.What they build: German maker of strain wave gears (the 'harmonic drive' zero-backlash gearbox used in most robot arm joints) and precision drive systems for robotics, medical, aerospace and space.
organizations._relationship_reason: Reference supplier for robot-joint gearboxes; useful as a speaker or factory visit on actuation; its parts are too expensive for a low-cost lab.

organizations.What they build: German family company for grippers, toolholding and workholding. In 2026 it signed a partnership with Bosch Robotics to co-design an industrial-grade robot hand for humanoid robots.
organizations._relationship_reason: Leading European gripper maker moving into humanoid hands; a talk or demo-gripper loan is plausible.

organizations.What they build: German automation supplier: pneumatic and electric actuators, motors and servo drives, grippers, vacuum, sensors, handling systems. Also runs Festo Didactic (technical education) and is known for bionic robot prototypes.
organizations._relationship_reason: Its education arm (Didactic) targets schools; possible training kits or a speaker. Bionic projects are good inspiration.

organizations.What they build: German 'motion plastics' company (self-lubricating plastic bearings, cable chains, linear axes). Sells the low-cost ReBeL cobot and robolink joints, and in 2025 launched Iggy Rob, a wheeled humanoid with two ReBeL arms and bionic hands priced at $54,500.
organizations._relationship_reason: Best fit of the slice: low-cost robot parts and arms aimed at makers; a sponsorship or discounted ReBeL arm/joints is realistic.

organizations.What they build: Danish maker of end-of-arm tooling for cobots: electric and vacuum grippers, force/torque sensors, tool changers, plus D:PLOY software for palletizing, CNC tending and packaging.
organizations._relationship_reason: Grippers fit popular cobots (UR etc.); loan of a gripper for a demo is plausible via distributors.

organizations.What they build: German chipmaker: power semiconductors (incl. GaN), microcontrollers and sensors for motor control, perception and safety in robots. Has a robotics development platform (Infineon Mobile Robot, IMR) and ran a 2026 Startup Challenge on humanoid robotics (100+ startups, won by AdapTronics). Partnered with Nvidia on humanoid robotics (Mar 2026).
organizations._relationship_reason: Actively courts robotics startups (startup challenge) and gives dev boards; realistic sponsor of motor-control boards or a challenge entry.

organizations.What they build: Franco-Italian chipmaker (HQ Geneva): STM32 microcontrollers, MEMS sensors (IMUs), motor drivers. In 2026 it took a stake in Italian humanoid maker Oversonic Robotics (RoBee) and partnered with Nvidia on sim-to-real robotics.
organizations._relationship_reason: Strong French presence; STM32 dev boards are cheap and ST has university programs; good candidate for boards and a speaker.

organizations.What they build: Dutch chipmaker: processors, sensing (radar, vision, UWB), Ethernet/TSN and CAN networking, security and functional safety for drones, AMRs and humanoids. Announced physical-AI work with Nvidia in Mar 2026.
organizations._relationship_reason: Has drone/rover dev kits and university programs; plausible source of eval boards.

organizations.What they build: Dutch edge-AI chip startup. Its Metis chip (~214 TOPS at ~10 W) uses digital in-memory computing to run vision models on robots and cameras. Raised more than $250M in Feb 2026 (led by Innovation Industries, with BlackRock and Samsung Catalyst).
organizations._relationship_reason: European alternative to Nvidia Jetson for on-robot inference; startups often give dev kits to visible student teams.

organizations.What they build: Italian open-source electronics platform (microcontroller boards + IDE), now a Qualcomm subsidiary. In 2026 it launched VENTUNO Q, its first board for robotics: Qualcomm Dragonwing IQ8 processor (40 TOPS) for AI plus an STM32H5 microcontroller for real-time motor control.
organizations._relationship_reason: Community-driven brand that sponsors maker events; a hackathon partnership or VENTUNO Q boards is realistic.

organizations.What they build: UK maker of low-cost Arm single-board computers (Raspberry Pi 5), Pico microcontroller boards (RP2 chips), cameras and add-on boards; widely used as the 'brain' of hobby and student robots.
organizations._relationship_reason: Cheap compute for every robot we build; a small hardware donation or featured content is plausible.

organizations.What they build: German industrial sensor maker: safety laser scanners, lidar, 2D/3D vision and other sensors used on AMRs and in factory automation.
organizations._relationship_reason: Safety lidar is standard on mobile robots; possible sensor loan or speaker on robot safety.

organizations.What they build: UK maker of the Shadow Dexterous Hand (tendon-driven, five-fingered research hand with tactile fingertips) and the DEX-EE hand. In Oct 2026 it started a six-month project with Fraunhofer IFF on dexterous hands, tactile sensing and teleoperation for manufacturing.
organizations._relationship_reason: Pioneer of dexterous hands; good for talks; hardware far too expensive.

organizations.What they build: Swiss ETH spin-off making compact 6-axis force-torque sensors (MiniONE, Rokubi, SensONE, LaxONE) with integrated electronics and IMU, plus tactile sensors, so robots can 'feel' contact forces.
organizations._relationship_reason: Startup selling to research and robot-learning teams; a discounted sensor for a contact-rich imitation-learning demo is plausible.

organizations.What they build: German maker of integrated servo drives, robot actuators and functional-safety motion control. Since Aug 2026 it co-develops and manufactures integrated humanoid joint actuators with Stabilus.
organizations._relationship_reason: Deep actuator and safety expertise; useful as mentor on motor control; hardware is industrial-priced.

organizations.What they build: Swiss physical-AI startup building robots with a sense of force and touch (haptic sensing) to improve dexterous manipulation, rethinking the stack from hardware to models. Exited stealth in Oct 2026 with a $30M pre-seed (redalpine, Notion Capital, firstminute; angels Arthur Mensch, Yann LeCun).
organizations._relationship_reason: Young, Paris-connected investors (Mensch, LeCun); founders could talk on force/touch for robot learning.

organizations.What they build: Hungarian startup automating the manufacture of robot bodies with '3D Tissue Braiding': it braids tendon-driven soft tissues around a scaffold so hands and limbs come out in one process. Raised a $7.2M pre-seed in Feb 2026 (OpenAI and Hugging Face angels reported).
organizations._relationship_reason: Early startup open to pilot users; possible partner for a custom hand/finger project.

organizations.What they build: Italian startup making electro-adhesive gripping pads (Electro Active Adhesive Layer) with tactile feedback: a thin film becomes sticky on command to grab objects of almost any shape without suction or fingers. Won Infineon's 2026 humanoid robotics Startup Challenge.
organizations._relationship_reason: Small startup; a demo partnership on a novel gripper is plausible.

summary: Leaders: German motion/automation incumbents (Schaeffler, maxon, Harmonic Drive, SCHUNK, Festo, igus) for actuators, gears and grippers, and the three European chipmakers (Infineon, ST, NXP) for motor control, sensors and compute.
Money: humanoid actuators are the hot spot (Schaeffler supplies and buys Humanoid robots; Synapticon-Stabilus; SCHUNK-Bosch hands); chipmakers all partnered with Nvidia in 2026.
Startups: touch/force sensing and hands draw funding (Enact $30M pre-seed, Bota, Allonic $7.2M, AdapTronics), plus edge AI chips (Axelera $250M+).
Demand: humanoid makers need cheap, reliable joints and hands; Europe positions itself as component supplier while China scales full robots.

Best entry point for 42AI: low-cost maker suppliers (igus, Arduino, Raspberry Pi, STMicroelectronics in France) for hardware sponsoring, and Infineon's startup challenge / Bota or Enact for force-sensing robot-learning demos.
